source.reasoning_observation: Affine calibration: two fixed points determine an offset and scale; the observed mapping gives 60 on the new scale. No independent exam qualification.

related_source_observations.reasoning_observation: Absolute temperature equals Celsius reading plus 273.15; 37.3 °C converts numerically to 310.45 K before rounding. A displayed tenth-degree reading does not warrant hundredth-degree measurement precision.

target.protected_work: Fit and independently test a two-point affine thermometer model, then separate absolute temperature, temperature interval and readout precision.
target.decisive_route: Two calibrations at 5 and45 °C read 20 and100. A reserved 25 °C reference reads 62. Test the affine model; if a sample reads 80, give conditional Celsius and Kelvin estimates. representation_translation.evidence: Translate reference measurements into two independent equations.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Fit slope/intercept; predict unused reading and compare interval conversion.

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: A fixed offset cancels in intervals but not absolute temperature.

core1a.scientific_construction: An affine scale is r=aθ+b, where θ is Celsius temperature and r is the readout. Two distinct reference temperatures determine a and b if the linear model applies. Subtract readings to remove the offset; use a third independent reference to test the assumption. Kelvin temperature is T=θ+273.15, but ΔT in kelvin equals Δθ in degrees Celsius. A conversion does not create measurement precision. A reading rounded to 0.1 °C has at least the stated rounding limitation; calibration and sensor response can add uncertainty. A systematic offset can leave a measured change correct while making absolute readings wrong.

worked_anchor.task: A sensor reads 8 and 68 at 10 °C and 40 °C. Find its affine relation and predicted readout at 25 °C.
worked_anchor.reasoning: Slope 2 units/°C; offset −12; predicted 38. An offset-only model cannot fit the two points.
